search_window.basis: Supplementary hourly recall, including previously unrecorded source-dated high-value items. Late-recalled events are not presented as occurring anew; primary Gaza production remains authoritative.

findings.title: Medical sources warn of continued reduction in number patients and wounded permitted to leave Gaza
findings.location: Gaza Strip; medical departures via Egypt (specific crossing procedure not independently confirmed)
findings.affected_population_or_system: Gaza patients awaiting external treatment and their companions. Unnamed medical sources quoted by WAFA say only 22 people, counting both patients and companions, were granted permission to travel on 17 November; the medical-evacuation backlog reportedly exceeded 21,000 patient cases. Sources claim departures are tied to the number of people returning from Egypt after treatment. Permissions are not verified completed evacuations.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: The medical sources stated that only 22 people—patients and their companions—were granted permission to travel today, Tuesday.
findings.source_type: Palestinian official news agency reporting statements attributed to unnamed medical sources; no independent manifest or WHO verification found

discovery_context.first_seen: Late-recovered during direct WAFA last-news review on November 18, after primary official checks and within the bounded search plan. Report publication and reported authorization date are November 17, well before the current observation window.
discovery_context.novelty: Specific single-day authorization cap of 22 people (patients plus companions), reported linkage of outbound permissions to Egypt returns, and >21,000-case patient backlog were not recorded as findings in the immediately preceding authenticated heartbeat or checked November 17 hourly findings. This quantifies ongoing medical-evacuation constraints rather than documenting a new crossing closure.
discovery_context.limitations: WAFA quotes unidentified medical sources; number authorized is not number actually evacuated, and number of patients is not 22 because companions are included. The claimed return-linked policy, underlying approval authority, and 21,000-case list were not independently verified; no WHO/OCHA announcement confirming a new policy identified.
